opening.text: On a cold night, a campfire changes everything. People pull their chairs in. Faces light up. Someone tells a story. Nobody planned it. The fire just drew them together. Joy in the gospel is like that fire. It warms us, and it draws others near.

mainMessage.text: Joy is a fire kept by Jesus Christ. It warms us and draws others close.

blocks.text: **Where the fire comes from** The fire isn't lit by our own effort alone. It comes from the Savior.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy comes from and because of Him.
He lights the fire.
**Made for the fire** We weren't made to sit in the cold. We were made to have joy.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
We were created to have joy.
We were made for joy.
**Strength in the heat** A fire gives light and strength. Joy does too.

Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is powerful, and focusing on joy brings God’s power into our lives.
Joy gives strength.
**Warmth isn't the same as ease** A fire is warm, but we still have to gather wood. Joy and comfort are not the same thing.

Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy. And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
But joy and comfort are not the same thing.
Joy isn't the same as comfort.
**A gift for the faithful** The fire is a gift. It stays lit for those who keep coming back.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is a gift for the faithful.
Keep coming back.
**He shares His fire** The Savior wants us to have joy. He doesn't keep it to Himself.
And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
He wants to share His joy with us.
He shares it.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt real joy, even in a hard season. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Alma's joy

blocks.text: Alma had carried deep pain over his sins. Then he turned to Jesus Christ.

And oh, what joy, and what marvelous light I did behold; yea, my soul was filled with joy as exceeding as was my pain! Yea, I say unto you, my son, that there could be nothing so exquisite and so bitter as were my pains. Yea, and again I say unto you, my son, that on the other hand, there can be nothing so exquisite and sweet as was my joy.
The pain was real, and so was the joy. The Savior took the one and gave the other.

application.text: First, think about what brings you true joy, not just fun. Second, make a little more room for it this week. Third, tell someone about it.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Jesus Christ is the source of joy. I know Heavenly Father made us to have it. I know joy can live in us even on hard days. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A kite doesn't rise by running against the wind. It rises because the wind lifts it. You hold the string. You let it climb. Joy is a lot like that. We can't make it by effort alone. It lifts us when we are in the right place, in the Savior's wind.

mainMessage.text: Joy is a wind that lifts us. We hold the string, and the Savior sends the wind.

blocks.text: **The wind comes from Him** The lift is His. We only need to open up.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy comes from and because of Him.
The wind is His.
**Built to fly** A kite is made to fly. We were made to have joy.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
We were created to have joy.
Made to rise.
**Power in the air** Wind has power. Joy has power too, and focusing on it brings God's strength.

Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is powerful, and focusing on joy brings God’s power into our lives.
It carries power.
**Wind isn't always calm** The best wind for a kite isn't a breeze. It has some force. Joy and comfort are not the same thing.

Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy. And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
But joy and comfort are not the same thing.
Joy can rise in hard wind.
**A gift for the string-holders** We hold on to the string by staying faithful. Joy is a gift for those who do.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is a gift for the faithful.
Hold on.
**He wants us up there** The Savior wants us to soar, not stay stuck. He wants to share His joy.
And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
He wants to share His joy with us.
Let Him lift you.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they felt lifted. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Good tidings of great joy

blocks.text: Shepherds were out in the fields at night. An angel appeared with news.
And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
The angel said the joy was for all people. It wasn't kept for a few. The birth of Jesus Christ is the reason joy is possible for each of us.

application.text: First, think of a burden you've been holding too tightly. Second, pray and let some of it go. Third, notice what lifts.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father wants us to rise. I know Jesus Christ lifts us when we turn to Him. I know joy is real, and it is for everyone. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A spring in the hills doesn't ask where the water goes. It just keeps flowing. Travelers stop and drink. Gardens grow downstream. The spring never runs dry because it is fed from deep below. Joy is like that. It flows from a source we can't see, and it feeds a lot more than us.

mainMessage.text: Joy is a spring. It flows from Jesus Christ, and it doesn't run dry.

blocks.text: **The source** Every spring has a source. For joy, it is the Savior.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy comes from and because of Him.
Go to the source.
**Meant to flow** We were created for this. Joy is part of the plan.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
We were created to have joy.
Meant to flow.
**Power in the water** A spring can turn a mill. Joy brings God's power into our lives.

Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is powerful, and focusing on joy brings God’s power into our lives.
It gives power.
**Water in a dry season** The best springs flow in dry seasons. Joy can too. It is not the same as comfort.

Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy. And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
But joy and comfort are not the same thing.
It flows in dry times.
**A gift to drink** The spring is a gift. We receive it by living faithfully.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is a gift for the faithful.
Drink and be grateful.
**Shared downstream** The Savior wants us to have His joy. And a spring that is shared grows gardens.
And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
He wants to share His joy with us.
Share it downstream.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when joy came from the Savior at a time they didn't expect it. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Lehi tastes the fruit

blocks.text: Lehi saw the tree of life in a dream. He tasted the fruit.

And it came to pass that I did go forth and partake of the fruit thereof; and I beheld that it was most sweet, above all that I ever before tasted. Yea, and I beheld that the fruit thereof was white, to exceed all the whiteness that I had ever seen. And as I partook of the fruit thereof it filled my soul with exceedingly great joy; wherefore, I began to be desirous that my family should partake of it also; for I knew that it was desirable above all other fruit.
Joy came, and with it a wish to share. Lehi didn't keep the fruit to himself. He wanted his family to taste it too.

application.text: First, think of a moment of real joy from your life. Second, ask what led you there. Third, do more of that, and share it with someone.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the joy of the Lord is real. I know Heavenly Father gives it to those who come to Him. I know Jesus Christ is the source. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A rainbow only shows up when rain and sun meet. If it were all sun, there would be no rainbow. If it were all rain, we wouldn't see one either. The best colors come when both are in the sky together. Joy is like that. It can shine right through our tears.

mainMessage.text: Joy can appear in the very sky where the rain is falling.

blocks.text: **The Light behind the color** A rainbow needs light. The light of joy is Jesus Christ.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy comes from and because of Him.
The Light is His.
**Made to see it** We weren't made only to endure the rain. We were made to have joy.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
We were created to have joy.
Made for joy.
**Strength in the storm** The rainbow rises where the storm is breaking. Joy gives strength then.

Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is powerful, and focusing on joy brings God’s power into our lives.
Joy brings strength.
**Rain and light together** Joy doesn't wait for the rain to stop. Joy and comfort are not the same thing.

Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy. And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
But joy and comfort are not the same thing.
Joy and rain can meet.
**A gift for those who stay** The ones who keep looking up see the rainbow. Joy is a gift for the faithful.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is a gift for the faithful.
Keep looking up.
**Pointing it out** When we see a rainbow, we call others to look. The Savior wants to share His joy with us, and we can share it with others.
And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
He wants to share His joy with us.
Point it out.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when joy came during a hard trial. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Ammon's joy

blocks.text: Ammon had faced danger and hardship on his mission. And yet he spoke of joy.
But Ammon said unto him: I do not boast in my own strength, nor in my own wisdom; but behold, my joy is full, yea, my heart is brim with joy, and I will rejoice in my God.
Ammon's joy wasn't about easy days. It was about what God had done. Joy that rests on Him can fill a heart even after hard times.

application.text: First, think of a trial you are in now. Second, look for one small thing in it that you can be glad about. Third, thank Heavenly Father for it out loud.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Savior turns sorrow into joy. I know Heavenly Father is with us in the storm. I know joy can fill a heart even when tears are falling. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A bell doesn't ring on its own. Something has to strike it. But once it rings, the sound goes out across the whole valley, and everyone who hears it knows something good has happened. Joy is a bell. When the Savior touches our hearts, it rings. And others hear it.

mainMessage.text: Joy is a bell the Savior rings in us. It carries farther than we expect.

blocks.text: **Who strikes the bell** The bell rings when the Savior touches us.
These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy comes from and because of Him.
He rings it.
**Cast to ring** A bell is made to ring. We were made for joy.
Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
We were created to have joy.
Made to ring.
**A sound with strength** A bell can be heard through fog. Joy has power that carries us through hard times.

Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is powerful, and focusing on joy brings God’s power into our lives.
It carries through fog.
**Ringing in a hard season** A bell can ring in a storm. Joy and comfort are not the same thing, and joy can ring in a hard season.

Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy. And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
But joy and comfort are not the same thing.
Ring in the storm.
**A gift for the faithful** The bell tower is kept up by faithful hands. Joy is a gift for the faithful.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, said this in his talk “Joy and Spiritual Survival” from the October 2016 general conference.
Joy is a gift for the faithful.
Keep the tower.
**Heard by others** A bell is meant to be heard. The Savior wants us to have His joy, and to share it.
And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves.
Elder Craig C. Christensen of the Seventy said this in his talk “There Can Be Nothing So Exquisite and Sweet as Was My Joy” from the April 2023 general conference.
He wants to share His joy with us.
Let it be heard.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when their joy touched someone else. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Paul and Silas sing in prison

blocks.text: Paul and Silas were in prison at midnight. They sang. A jailer heard them.

And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them. And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
Their joy rang out from a cell. The jailer heard it. He and his whole family came to believe and rejoiced.

application.text: First, think of a way you can let your joy be seen this week. Second, share a kind word, a song or a smile. Third, notice who hears it.

blocks.text: I know Jesus Christ is joy. I know Heavenly Father gives it to those who seek Him. I know joy that is shared grows. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
